purpose: Certify a DIRECTIONAL-accuracy claim for the simulator on the IN-SCOPE deliberative-product-change class, across a curated set of WHOLE-EXPERIMENT cases (each = one real A/B with a known published winner). The unit of evidence is a whole experiment (see BENCHMARK_REPORT.md sec 6); Cookie Cats is case #1 (correct). This portfolio supplies the other independent cases needed to clear the 8-case null-cert floor with GENUINELY independent bits (not re-slices of one experiment).

methodology.structural_reality: No public source has NAMED treatments + raw per-user data + in-scope product change together (NeurIPS 2021 Liu et al. survey confirms). Cookie Cats is the rare raw-data anchor; all other cases are published narratives with point-estimate outcomes. So the harness scores the sim against the REPORTED winner/direction, not by re-analyzing rows.
methodology.must_run_the_engine: The sim's claim is that simulating an AUDIENCE yields the right aggregate. So each case MUST be run through the real agent-simulation engine on a rendered control-vs-treatment stimulus, BLINDED to the outcome. Simply asking an LLM 'which wins?' is INVALID — it measures memorization, not the product.
methodology.scoring: direction_accuracy (sign agreement: did the sim pick the real winner?) is the headline. Magnitude is OUT of scope for narrative/vendor cases (point estimates are inflated by publication bias). rank_rho across cases where effect sizes are credible (peer-reviewed/first-party only). Null-integrity certificate required (>=8 cases, label variation).
publication_bias_mitigations: BALANCE: keep ~40% control-won cases so a sim that always predicts 'the change wins' cannot score well by default. Current scored set: 8 cases, control-won = Office Online, MSN offers, CXL form-fields, Cookie Cats (gate_30=control wins) = 4/8 = 50%.
DIRECTION-ONLY scoring for vendor/CRO showcases (effect sizes inflated).
Report as 'directional accuracy on a HARD, curated set', NOT a population estimate.
HUMAN BASELINE anchor: Kohavi's expert survey ~2.3/8 correct; MSN Real-Estate widget 3/21 experts predicted the winner. Position the sim against these.
ALWAYS pull the PRIMARY source's number before scoring (secondary retellings miscite, e.g. Etsy -22%/-50%, Highrise 47% vs 37.5%).
methodology.contamination_control: Famous results an LLM may have memorized are HELD OUT of the scored set into a separate memorization probe. If the sim aces the famous ones but flunks the obscure ones, it is reciting, not reasoning.
methodology.narrative_normalization_v2: 2026-06-17, AFTER the v1 scored run (dir_acc 0.25, pro-change tilt 7/8). A read-only adapter audit found the engine RENDERING path is arm-symmetric, BUT the authored control/treatment NARRATIVES carried arm-asymmetric VALENCE (treatment described with benefit/positive words: 'more appealing', 'preserves the streak', 'simplest/simplified') and one OUTCOME LEAK ('winner of 6 variants' in msn_realestate's treatment — a direct answer leak the blindness test missed because 'winner' != 'won'). Since the adapter passes these strings VERBATIM into the blinded stimulus, the asymmetry reached the model. v2 NORMALIZES both arms to neutral, parallel, mechanic-only descriptions (strip evaluative adjectives + outcome hints from BOTH arms symmetrically; do NOT flip valence toward control = no over-correction; preserve the factual mechanic of each change). real_winner/effect/etc are unchanged ground-truth (never rendered). This is an INTEGRITY FIX; the v1 result is preserved (portfolio_results.txt) and the v2 re-run is reported as a clean replication that separates copy-valence artifact from genuine model prior. Registered prediction (from the audit): dir_acc stays near chance; the 7/8 treatment-rate drops toward ~5/8.

scored_cases.control: The first forced progress gate is at level 30.
scored_cases.treatment: The first forced progress gate is at level 40.
scored_cases.status: ALREADY RUN (2026-06-17): clean by-arm dir_acc 1.0 (sign RIGHT) but VOID at n=1; this portfolio gives it company.

scored_cases.control: Missing a day of practice ends the user's streak.
scored_cases.treatment: An equippable 'Weekend Amulet' item keeps the streak active through one skipped weekend day.
scored_cases.counter_intuitive: high (a skip-day safety valve 'should' weaken the habit loop; it raised return)

scored_cases.treatment: A redesigned 'Find a home' widget with a search-box-style layout.
scored_cases.counter_intuitive: high (only 3/21 experts predicted the winner; richer designs were the prior)
scored_cases.credibility: high (Kohavi DMCS 2009, peer-recognized); carries a HUMAN BASELINE 3/21
scored_cases.source: Kohavi et al., Online Experimentation at Microsoft (DMCS 2009)

scored_cases.control: The existing Buy page; the price is shown.
scored_cases.treatment: A redesigned Buy page with a different layout; the price is not shown.
scored_cases.caveat: Kohavi flags as FLAWED-OEC: treatment HID price so 'clicks' is the wrong metric. Score sim on the STATED metric (clicks -> control) and DISCLOSE the confound.

scored_cases.treatment: The MSN homepage with 3 additional paid offers placed below the shopping module.
scored_cases.counter_intuitive: med-high (marketing projected big gains; clutter cost net money)

scored_cases.control: The card application requires passport details at step 2.
scored_cases.treatment: The card application adds a 'Don't remember? Add later' checkbox that defers the passport field to a later step.
scored_cases.counter_intuitive: med (letting a required field be skipped feels risky)
scored_cases.credibility: med (VWO showcase; large n + significance) -- DIRECTION-only scoring

scored_cases.treatment: A 6-field form (three of the nine fields removed).
scored_cases.counter_intuitive: high ('fewer fields always win' is near-universal)
scored_cases.credibility: med (CXL/Aagaard; client anonymized but plain-words describable) -- DIRECTION-only

scored_cases.effect: more steps (6) won; re-adding a step recovered conversion
scored_cases.counter_intuitive: high (fewer steps is the textbook answer; it lost)
scored_cases.note: real_winner=control means the FEWER-steps treatment LOST; control(6-step) won. Double-check primary source phrasing at build time.

held_out_memorization_probe.change: registration wall -> let prospects browse catalog first (5 variants)
held_out_memorization_probe.real_winner: control (won all 5); 46% SAID they wanted browsing
held_out_memorization_probe.why_held_out: high contamination (textbook stated-vs-revealed-preference inversion, widely retold)

held_out_memorization_probe.change: long info-dense page -> short page w/ big real-customer photo + simple signup
held_out_memorization_probe.real_winner: treatment (+47% paid signups; adding content back = -22%)

balance_check.note: Slightly control-heavy; a naive 'change always wins' sim scores <=3/8. Good. If we add more treatment-won obscure cases later, keep >=40% control-won.

further_sources.more_named_cases: Kohavi/Tang/Xu corpus: DMCS 2009 (Online Experimentation at Microsoft), Trustworthy Online Controlled Experiments (2020), Five Puzzling Outcomes Explained (KDD 2012), Online Controlled Experiments at Large Scale (KDD 2013). Filter OUT SERP/ranking cases (out of scope). High contamination, no raw data.
further_sources.dataset_map: Liu et al., Datasets for Online Controlled Experiments, NeurIPS 2021 (arXiv:2111.10198) -- enumerates all 13 public OCE datasets; confirms named+raw+in-scope does not co-exist publicly. ASOS = anonymized (useless). Upworthy = headline copy, group-level (already a null for us).
